sentences.text: Offences complained of U/S 498A and 304B of IPC and Section 3 and 4  of DP Act Opinion of the Judge Accused found guilty for  the offences PUS 498A  and 306 of IPC  JUDGMENT The Assistant Commissioner of police K.R.Puram Sub-division has filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/sec.498A and 304B of IPC along with sec. 3 and 4 of DP act.

2. The gist of the prosecution case is under; The marriage of the deceased Smt. Sunanda daughter of CW-1 was solemnized with the accused on 30-01-2005 at Sethu Ram Kalyan Mantapa Bengaluru as per the customs prevailing in their community.
It is alleged that, at the time of marriage the accused on demand has received cash of Rs.30,000-00 with gold ornaments as dowry from her parents.
After the marriage the accused forced his wife to reside in his native village Kodiganahalli in Hindupura Andhra Pradesh with her parents in law.

Though he led conjugal life with his wife for nearly 4 years in different houses situated in RPN area, Girinagar and lastly in Ramamurthynagar Bengaluru he allegedly harassed his wife to bring additional dowry of Rs.5 lakhs to clear his debts and thrown out her with two children from matrimonial home.
However after settlement before the JMFC II court Mysore in C.Misc.No.99/2009 against to his own undertaking given before said court he continuously harassed his deceased wife from 11-06- 2009.

4. On 02-10-2009 the accused after beating his wife in the morning had gone outside with his two children, the deceased Smt. Sunanda being fed up with dowry harassment has committed suicide by hanging self with ceiling fan in matrimonial home bearing H.No.302 in an apartment situated in Hoysalanagar.
Hence, the prosecution has alleged that, the accused has committed the offences described above.

5. The investigating officer has filed the charge sheet before the learned X ACMM Court Bengaluru and said court after compliance with provisions of section 207 of Cr.P.C. since the offence PUS 304B of IPC is SC No.156/2010 exclusively triable by a Sessions Court said court has committed the case.
Firstly the case was pending on the file of learned FTC-X Bengaluru then it was made over to the court of XLIV ACC & SJ Bengaluru and lastly made over to this court.
The accused is on bail and represented by the counsel Sri SS throughout the proceedings.

6. The following points arise for consideration:
1. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that, the accused at the time of marriage with deceased Smt. Sunanda on 30-01-2005 has received cash Rama Murthy Nagar Ps vs Ramanjaneyalu Ramanjaneyalu on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77823646/

In the absence of reliable evidence such as any document only on the basis of oral evidence of PW-1 to 3 the demand and receipt of dowry of Rs.30,000- 00 at the time of marriage cannot be said to be established by the prosecution.

30. The learned Public Prosecutor has argued that, the prosecution has relied on oral evidence of 9 witnesses and equal number of documents with MO-1 thereby it has discharged the burden to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt for the offences alleged against him as such prayed to convict the accused for the offences PUS 498A and 304B of IPC along with sections 3 and 4 of DP Act.

Since the learned counsel for accused has relied on numerous citations and argued for acquittal SC No.156/2010 of accused the learned PP has submitted that, none of the citations are applicable to the facts of this case.

31. The prosecution has alleged that, at the time of marriage the accused has received cash of Rs.30,000-00 and gold jewelry and to prove this it has mainly relies on oral evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and the contents of Ex.P-1.
Of course, they have reiterated about this in chief as well as cross examination which is in conformity with contents of Ex.P-1.

But in cross examination they have,
particularly PW-1, repeatedly admitted that, there is custom in their family to give gold jewelry to the bride groom at the time of marriage.
As she has given gold jewelry to her other three sons-in-law by following said practice she has given gold jewelry to accused at the time of marriage with her deceased daughter.

When there is clear evidence on record which speaks of the fact that, whatever jewelry given to son-in-law i.e., accused, was as per the customary practice in the family then where is the scope to believe that, the accused has received it as dowry after demand.
A meaningful reading of cross examination portion of PW-1 clearly reveals that, she has given the ornaments to the accused as per customs.
So it cannot be said that, the accused had demanded and received the jewelry at the time of marriage with the deceased.

In so far as the payment of cash of Rs.30,000- 00 by PW-1 to the accused at the time of marriage as dowry in fact there is no acceptable and reliable evidence on record except oral testimony of PW-1 to 3 as such on the basis of mere oral assertions it cannot be believed that, the accused has really received cash of Rs.30,000- 00 from PW-1 as dowry.
On the other hand the accused in his oral evidence as DW-1 has also vehemently denies about receiving of cash of Rs.30,000-00 at the time of marriage.

Looking to the oral evidence of PW-1 and DW- 1 it appears that, this is oath against oath and only on the strength of oral assertions it is not possible to believe that, the prosecution has proved that, the accused has received cash of Rs,30,000-00 at the time of marriage as dowry from his in laws.

sentences.text: Thus for the discussion made above I am of the opinion that, the prosecution has failed to prove the allegations of dowry demand and receipt of cash of Rs.30,000-00 with jewelry by the accused from his parents-in-law.

34. The learned counsel Sri SS has vehemently argued that even before registering the case as per Ex.P-1 the IO had visited the place of crime and had enquired with the witnesses and after deliberations he registered the case as such the same cannot be treated as SC No.156/2010 complaint U/S 154 of Cr.P.C. as such it is hit by section 162 of Cr.P.C.
In support of his arguments the learned counsel has relied on oral evidence of PW-1, PW-2 particularly his admissions under Ex.D-3.

The learned counsel has also relied on the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court and also of Our Own Hon'ble High Court Karnataka as follows;
a. Between State of AP Vs Punati Ramulu and others reported in AIR 1993 SC 2644.
b. Between H C Karigowda @ Srinivasa and others Vs State of Karnataka repotted in ILR 2013 KAR 992.
35.

sentences.text: Before forming any opinion in relation to applicability of these two citations it is just and necessary to narrate the facts of this case post the death of Smt. Sunanda.
It is true that, PW-2 as per the statement recorded by Spl. Tahsildar had first gone to the police station and thereafter he visited the scene of crime along with the police.

Since the PSI of Ramamurthynagar has not been examined and in absence of his evidence as well in the absence of evidence to show that, the police who visited the spot was said PSI or any other police official that is not clarified in their evidence.
It is relevant to note that, PW-2 had already received information of harassment to deceased by the accused in the morning on 02-10-2009 but did not expected that she would end her life.
But when he heard the news of unnatural death SC No.156/2010 of his sister's daughter he felt it would be safer to go to police station first and then to the house of deceased.
Moreover in cognizable offence the police before registering the case for confirmation may visit the scene of crime.

But there is no proof to show that, the police official who had visited the spot with PW-2 even prior to registration of the case had made enquiry with the witnesses or had any deliberation in relation to the Crime.
Under such circumstances the defense arguments that prior to registration of the case the IO had visited the scene of crime made enquiry and deliberations with the witnesses cannot be accepted.

36. In the given citations the situation was altogether different as the police officer had visited the spot and made enquiry with the witnesses and thereafter registered the case as such the Hon'ble Apex Court and also Our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has been pleased to hold that, in a such a situation the complaint cannot be treated as first information as contemplated U/S 154 of Cr.P.C.
Since the facts of the instant case are different from the facts discussed in the above judgments as such the above two judgments are not applicable to this case.

Therefore, I hold that, Ex.P-1 is purely a complaint as such it is not hit by section 162 of Cr.P.C. Hence, I am of the opinion that, Ex.P-1 is not hit by section 162 of Cr.P.C.
